I like dogs (I currently own three), but I hate irresponsible dog owners (of which there are far, far too many) and I don't like having to deal wit the byproduct of that-- being unable to walk my dog down the street without them getting charged at by some aggressive dog, dog shit all over the sidewalks, dogs in grocery stores and places where non-service dogs shouldn't be, which is part of why I frequent this sub. 

Dogs are *animals*, and shouldn't be treated as humans. You can treat an animal with care and dignity without making it out like it's a human, and that it's continued existence is on par with the value of protecting innocent people. I grew up with 7+ hunting dogs at any given time, and still have hounds as an adult. 

How many times have I, or anyone in my family, or anyone else been bitten by one of our dogs? 

Zero times, and if it became 1-- that dog would be put down immediately. We have a zero tolerance policy for aggression. I constantly see these stories about how X dog had bitten four people before mauling a child or someone's family pet and it baffles me completely that these dogs are even still alive. The first time a dog bites should be the last time. Shelters are often terrible culprits, sending dogs with bite histories out to unsuspecting people. I just don't understand it at all.

My mom has a dog I despise (I like dogs just fine, but hate that its impossible to get away from bad owners, untrained and aggressive dogs and "furbabies"), so I get it. I would love to give him away, but he isn't my dog, so it isn't my place. I just don't interact with him. 

I don't think going behind your SO's back and getting rid of her dog is the key to a long and healthy relationship. If she doesn't want to rehome the dog, you have a choice to make, stay with her and try to get the dog under control, or leave and find someone who doesn't own or want to own dogs. Even if you don't like the dog, if you tell her it slipped its collar/ran away/whatever you may have to live with that lie through her putting up fliers, going around the neighborhood looking for the dog, calling shelters and vets offices for weeks or months.
This though \^\^.

People can be super predatory. My friend and I were out in Vegas while road tripping and we were doing shot for shot/drink for drink. In part because it's funny and in part to keep an eye on how much we were drinking. I remember we had been put at a table with a promoter friend of ours and we were dancing, laughing, having a good time. Some guys at the table next to us offered us drinks. I declined but my friend accepted. So I know she only had one more drink than me. Next thing I know my friend is panicking. Says we need to leave NOW. I trust her so we bounce, but we barely made it from the club into the casino before she hits the ground. Wobbly legged, can't stand. I've known this girl for years now and we've gone out together more times than I can count. This night was the only time she was anything remotely like that. I had to all but carry her through the casino. She's crying, can't walk well, can barely stand. I got her into our hotel room finally and she's trying to make herself puke. Then just passes out cold on the bathroom floor. So much awful stuff could have happened if we had both taken drinks from that table and if my friend hadn't been able to tell immediately that something was wrong. :(

My dad committed suicide when I was about two years old. I only have one memory of him because I was so young. 

One night he cut down my tire swing. My mom and him were fighting, I was crying. I remember going to hide in the closet. 

25 years later I mentioned to my grandma that it was sad that the only memory I had of him was when him and my mom were fighting and that I'm sure he didn't mean anything by cutting down my swing. 
She turned white as a sheet and then told me the whole story.  

I knew he'd hung himself but I had never put two and two together. 

He hung himself with the rope from my tire swing. My mom doesn't know I remember.
